label: Person
name: Agostino Marchetto
summary:
Agostino Marchetto (b. 1940) is an Italian Catholic bishop and Vatican historian who served as Secretary of the Pontifical Council for the Pastoral Care of Migrants and Itinerant People, while becoming internationally known as a critic of certain interpretations of the Second Vatican Council. Ordained a priest of the Diocese of Vicenza and later a Vatican diplomat, he served as apostolic nuncio to multiple countries before his curial appointment.

Marchetto's scholarly reputation rests primarily on his 2005 book 'The Second Vatican Ecumenical Council: A Counterpoint for the History of the Council,' which contested the hermeneutic of rupture—the interpretation of Vatican II as a decisive break with the pre-conciliar Church. He argued for a 'hermeneutic of reform in continuity,' a position later endorsed by Pope Benedict XVI in his famous 2005 Christmas address to the Roman Curia. Marchetto's work provided scholarly substance to the conservative-reformist reading of the council.

His pastoral responsibility for migrants and itinerant peoples represented a different dimension of his ministry: the social and spiritual care of some of the Church's most vulnerable populations. He engaged issues of migration, trafficking, and the pastoral needs of seafarers, circus workers, pilgrims, and nomadic peoples. His career combined scholarly engagement with the council's hermeneutics and practical advocacy for marginalised communities.
